source.quote: Shanling's own product page for the M1, read 2026-11-25 - one of four with text. Main specifications: « Sampling rate: 44.1kHz--192kHz »; « D/A converter: AK4452 »; « Amplifier: MAX97220 »; « Referenced clock jitter: 200 femtosencond » (the page's spelling); « External memory: supported up to 256G TF card »; « WindowsXP/Windows7,8, 10(32/64bit), MAC OS X10.7 or the later version ». In the « Format Support » table, a row of its own: « DAC / supported up to 192kHz--24bit » and « DSD / DSD64、DSD128 ».

_la_source_est_une_annonce_ou_un_manuel_: Shanling's product pages are image-only, so every figure comes from the maker's own announcement at /article/NNNNNN or from its manual PDF, both on en.shanling.com. No number was read off an image, and nothing is sourced to store.shanling.com. See the brand file.
_ni_DoP_ni_natif_ne_sont_dits_pour_ce_mo: DoP appears on no Shanling page or manual, and « native » only in the UA dongle manuals and in EM5. Neither is stated for this model.
_le_rang_DAC_du_tableau_EST_le_mode_entr: « DAC / supported up to 192kHz--24bit » sits in the Format Support table beside a line naming Windows and macOS driver versions - so that row describes the USB DAC mode, and inputs.usb takes it. The main « Sampling rate: 44.1kHz--192kHz » row is playback. One page, two roles, each with its own figure, on a 2016 product - which this maker stopped doing the moment its pages became pictures.
_44_1_a_192_est_une_PLAGE: « Sampling rate: 44.1kHz--192kHz » is a range of rates, not a depth and a rate. The double hyphen makes it legible where Musical Fidelity's V90-DAC wrote the same shape as « 32-bit/192 kHz » and made it a trap. Noted because the M3s page, from the same maker, writes « 44.1kHz--384kHz » in a row that has run two table cells together, and there the shape is the only thing that saves it.
